newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees EMU on time, no comment on German gold.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees EMU on time, no comment on German gold.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said European leaders show a strong commitment to creating a single currency by the January 1, 1999, target date but declined to comment on a controversial plan to revalue German gold reserves as part of that effort.

"My impression is that there's a very strong commitment on the part of both political leaders and finance ministers to accomplish this," Rubin said. "Obviously there are challenges they're going to have to meet as evidenced from the news in the last couple of days."
Rubin, at a briefing, added that a strong Europe is good for the United States and in that context endorsed the plan for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

"I think that what is good for Europe is basically good for us, and if it is their view that an EMU is good for them, then therefore, in my view at least, (it is) also good for us," Rubin said. "I think they will continue on the track to try to put that in place on time."
Rubin was asked about Germany's plan to boost the recorded value of its gold reserves to 60 percent of market value, which would help it meet the public debt criteria for joining EMU.
"I don't have a view on that, I really don't," he replied.
